title: Bharata's journey
hook: the son a mother schemed for turns on her, and then has to convince another mother he never wanted any of it

segments.voice: Yesterday: your line, she thinks it's good news. Bharata came home to a silent city, and Kaikeyi told him the throne was his.

Kaikeyi has been waiting for this conversation: her son home, the crown ready. What she gets is fury. Bharata doesn't thank her. He tells her she has destroyed the family, killed his father with grief, and sent away the brother he loves. The kingdom she won for him, he says, he will never accept. Then he walks out, to face the person he dreads most: Kausalya, Rama's mother.
screen: `NO THANKS, ONLY GRIEF.` → `I WILL NEVER ACCEPT IT.` → `NOW, KAUSALYA.`

segments.voice: Kausalya has every reason to suspect him. Here is the son who gains everything from her son's exile. She says so, bitterly: you wanted the kingdom, now you have it. Take me to Rama too. Bharata falls at her feet and swears. Valmiki gives him a long chain of oaths, each naming a wrong he'd rather be guilty of than this. May I carry the guilt of one who betrays a trust, who strikes a sleeping person, who turns away a guest, if I ever wanted Rama gone. On and on, a son emptying himself out. Kausalya believes him. She takes his head in her lap, and they weep together. Then the duty that can't wait. Under Vasishtha's guidance, Bharata performs his father's funeral rites. The body is taken from the oil, the fire is lit, the queens and the city mourn, and the family offers water at the Sarayu. Afterward, at the palace, Shatrughna catches Manthara, the maid who started it all, and starts to drag her. Bharata stops him: Rama would never forgive us. And so the week closes. A hut on a green hill. A king's confession: a sound in the dark, a water pot, a father's curse. A death past midnight. A boy with no name who became Shravan Kumar. And a son called home without being told, who refuses the prize.
screen: `KAUSALYA'S SUSPICION.` · `A CHAIN OF OATHS.` · `THE KING'S LAST RITES.` · `THE WEEK, FROM THE TOP.` · then, large: `HE REFUSES THE PRIZE.`

segments.voice: Think of a time someone suspected you of something you didn't do, or you suspected someone who turned out innocent, and notice where it sits in your body: the jaw, the chest, the stomach. Breathe into that spot, and let each out-breath loosen it a little, the way Kausalya's suspicion loosened.
Bharata's journey. He rejects his mother's gift, swears his innocence to Kausalya, and performs his father's last rites.
Your line: he refuses the prize. In the end, Rama's mother believes him. That's day five hundred forty-six.

chat.says: Did Bharata want the throne his mother got for him?
options: No. He refused it and swore to Kausalya he never wanted Rama gone.
Yes, at first, until Kausalya shamed him into giving it up later.
He took it, but only to keep it safe until his father recovered.
chat.meaning: Bharata rebuked Kaikeyi, refused the kingdom, and swore oath after oath to Kausalya until she believed him.
